text:
maya: Spotting a spike in fncall validation rejects that rerouted to degen and were billed. Console shows quota blip during the canary. cc @raj @tammy

alex: Which validator was in canary?

maya: fncall-typed-strict (canary started yesterday). Most rejections are small coercion issues (arrays vs objects, missing optional meta). Router logs: ```2026-03-24T14:05:11Z WARN validator=fncall-typed-strict fncall=tool.notify status=REJECT reason=CoercionRefused details=\"field 'recipients' expected object, got array\"
2026-03-24T14:05:11Z INFO router reroute=degen-fallback billing_tag=charged```

raj: Oof. Reroute should not bill for validation failures. Looks like policy matrix maps any REJECT -> reroute+charge.

sam: Also we don't distinguish PARTIAL vs HARD in metrics; ops can't tell if these are fatal.

tammy: Quick mitigation: rollback to soft canary and patch router policy to set charge:false for validation reroutes.

maya: Rolling back: `/rollout set validator:fncall-typed-strict=soft-canary --id=canary-17`

deployer-bot: @maya received request. Applying...

deployer-bot: Done. 35% traffic.

sam: I'll open a small policy PR to add `charge: false` when reason matches CoercionRefused|SchemaMismatch.

raj: We should also add telemetry: labels validation_severity=hard|partial and billed_reroute_total. Add an alert when billed_reroute_total / reroute_total > 0.001 during canary windows.

tammy: I'll add dashboard panel and alert. Query draft: `sum(reroute_total) by (validator, route_id)`, `sum(billed_reroute_total) by (validator, route_id)` then compute ratio.

alex: Long-term: make adapters emit a permissive coercion flag and have strict validator optionally accept common coercions as soft rejects instead of hard. Add e2e test to CI for coercion behavior.

maya: Action items: 1) maya rolled canary -> soft (done). 2) sam PR for policy patch (ETA 1h). 3) tammy dashboard + alert (ETA EOD). 4) alex spec adapter/coercion tests (ETA next week). 5) raj update rollout checklist to call out billing semantics.

sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5009 - adds policy rule + unit test ensuring charge=false for validation reroutes.

tammy: Dashboard panel added to draft. Will request review.

raj: Customer impact check: ~1200 rerouted calls billed across 4 accounts during the 40m spike. Low dollar but we'll prepare credits if CS asks.

maya: Tammy, please prepare support template.

tammy: On it.

alex: After policy lands, let's run synthetic test that sends known coercion case and confirm router log shows billing_tag=free or charge=false and trace contains original payload sample id.

maya: Agreed. Also add note to rollout doc: "When enabling strict validators, ensure reroute paths are non-billable and monitoring is live."

raj: Fine. Re-enable strict only if billed_reroute_ratio < 0.01% for 1 hour and no CS complaints.

sam: Monitoring it now. Ping me if you see anything else. :thumbsup:
